title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche, ms. p. 713). Γ acts, as Galois or outer data, on a connected object 𝔛 with base point x0 and Π = π1(𝔛, x0). A connected Galois étale cover 𝔛' of 𝔛 with group M (a quotient of Π stable under Γ) is to be descended or twisted. The Γ-action gives an extension (287): 1 → M → M̃ → Γ → 1.

Previous page. The fibre functor 𝔛' ↦ E = 𝔛'(x0) gives an equivalence between the category of such 𝔛' and the category of pairs (E, θ), where:
- E is an M-torsor;
- θ: M̃ → Aff_Γ(E) is a morphism of extensions (289), inducing the identity on M.

This page.
(i) Automorphisms of an object are the 'translations' of E by elements of M^Γ = Cent(M̃) ∩ M that are compatible with θ, i.e. those coming from Aff_Γ(E).
(ii) Isomorphism classes of objects correspond bijectively to M-conjugacy classes of splittings of (287).
(iii) Precisely, there is a canonical M-equivariant map (290) E → Scind(M̃/Γ). It sends e to the section s_e(γ) = the unique lift g of γ with θ(g)(e) = e. The lifts of γ form an M-coset, and M acts simply transitively on E, so exactly one lift fixes e. Since a stabiliser is a subgroup, s_e is a homomorphism. Equivariance: s_{me} = m·s_e·m⁻¹.
(iv) The image of (290) is a single M-conjugacy class, the one attached to the isomorphism class.
(v) The map factors through M^Γ\E, giving the bijection (291).
(vi) Hence if M^Γ = 0, E is recovered canonically as the conjugacy class of splittings. By the next page, M̃ then acts on it by conjugation.

Next page. Corollary: if H^0(Γ̃, M) = H^1(Γ̃, M) = 0, the category is rigid. Isomorphism classes then correspond to data that are subsequently matched with certain quotient groups.

Modern restatement: M̃-sets on which M acts simply transitively are the sets M̃/H with H a complement of M. They are classified by conjugacy classes of complements, i.e. of splittings. This is the group-theoretic core of descent for Galois covers and of the 'sections ↔ forms of covers' dictionary used around the section conjecture.
errors: (291) is written with target all of Scind(M̃ ext. de Γ par M). The correct target is the single M-conjugacy class that is the image of (290), as the text itself says one line earlier.

The fibre of (290) over s_e is the centraliser of s_e(Γ) in M, i.e. M^{Γ via s_e}. This equals the section-independent group M^Γ = Cent(M̃) ∩ M only when M is abelian (or under extra hypotheses). For nonabelian M, quotienting by M^Γ alone is not right in general. The Corollary's H^0/H^1 hypothesis implicitly places us in the abelian or Γ̃-module setting.
Side-sided issue: automorphisms of an M-torsor are translations on the other side (by the opposite group). The notes gloss over this.

ideas.what: Category of forms/descents of a Galois cover with group M is equivalent to pairs (M-torsor E, morphism of extensions M̃ → Aff_Γ(E)), via the fibre functor
ideas.modern_name: Galois descent for torsors / Galois-categorical description of twisted forms
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (exposés V, XIII) in spirit; the specific formulation is unsure

ideas.what: Isomorphism classes ↔ M-conjugacy classes of splittings of 1→M→M̃→Γ→1; fibre E ≅ the conjugacy class modulo the centraliser
ideas.modern_name: Complements/sections of a group extension classify transitive M̃-sets free over M; nonabelian H^1 (first cohomology) and conjugacy classes of sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group theory / Serre; used systematically in the anabelian section-conjecture literature
ideas.where_published: Closely related to the 1983 letter to Faltings (sections ↔ points); this precise formulation is unsure

deep.surprise_reason: Standard dictionary between descent data for a Galois cover and conjugacy classes of splittings of the associated extension. It is carefully worked out but classical; minor slips only.
transcription_corrections: 'binaires [?]' is probably 'biunivoquement' (correspondent biunivoquement aux classes de M-conjugaison).
'scindages [?]' is confirmed: 'Scind' in (290)/(291) means the set of splittings (scindages).
In (291) the arrow is a bijection (↔) and the struck word '[morph.]' is replaced by 'isomorph.' — consistent with the image.

The phrase transcribed 'ilts [?] ... automorph.' likely reads roughly 'eux-mêmes automorphismes' or similar. It is illegible; the sense is that the relevant elements of M^Γ are those coming from Aff_Γ(E).
